sanskrit: yat tu kutsayase yodhān yudhyamānān yathābalam atra te varṇayiṣyāmi yathā yuddham avartata
english: As for your reviling of the warriors who fought with all their strength, I shall now describe to you how the battle truly unfolded.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā karṇaṃ tu putrās te bhīmasenaparājitam nāmṛṣyanta maheṣvāsāḥ sodaryāḥ pañca māriṣa
english: When they saw Karṇa worsted by Bhīmasena, your five sons, born of the same mother and mighty archers, could not endure it, O honored one.

sanskrit: durmarṣaṇo duḥsahaś ca durmado durdharo jayaḥ pāṇḍavaṃ citrasaṃnāhās taṃ pratīpam upādravan
english: Durmarṣaṇa, Duḥsaha, Durmada, Durdhara, and Jaya, splendid in their armor, rushed against that son of Pāṇḍu to oppose him.

sanskrit: te samantān mahābāhuṃ parivārya vṛkodaram diśaḥ śaraiḥ samāvṛṇvañ śalabhānām iva vrajaiḥ
english: Surrounding the mighty-armed Vṛkodara on every side, they veiled the quarters with arrows, as though with swarms of locusts.

sanskrit: āgacchatas tān sahasā kumārān devarūpiṇaḥ pratijagrāha samare bhīmaseno hasann iva
english: As those princes, fair as the gods, came swiftly on, Bhīmasena received them in battle as though with a laugh.

sanskrit: tava dṛṣṭvā tu tanayān bhīmasenasamīpagān abhyavartata rādheyo bhīmasenaṃ mahābalam
english: But seeing your sons drawn close to Bhīmasena, Rādheya advanced against the mighty Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: visṛjan viśikhān rājan svarṇapuṅkhāñ śilāśitān taṃ tu bhīmo 'bhyayāt tūrṇaṃ vāryamāṇaḥ sutais tava
english: Loosing shafts with golden nocks, whetted on stone, O king, he came on; and Bhīma rushed at him at once, though held back by your sons.

sanskrit: kuravas tu tataḥ karṇaṃ parivārya samantataḥ avākiran bhīmasenaṃ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ
english: Then the Kurus, encircling Karṇa on all sides, covered Bhīmasena with arrows of smooth-jointed shafts.

sanskrit: tān bāṇaiḥ pañcaviṃśatyā sāśvān rājan nararṣabhān sasūtān bhīmadhanuṣo bhīmo ninye yamakṣayam
english: With twenty-five arrows, O king, Bhīma of the fearsome bow sent those bull-like men, together with their horses and charioteers, to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: prāpatan syandanebhyas te sārdhaṃ sūtair gatāsavaḥ citrapuṣpadharā bhagnā vāteneva mahādrumāḥ
english: Lifeless, they fell from their chariots together with their charioteers, like great flowering trees laden with bright blossoms, broken by the wind.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma bhīmasenasya vikramam saṃvāryādhirathiṃ bāṇair yaj jaghāna tavātmajān
english: There we beheld the wondrous valor of Bhīmasena, who, while warding off the son of Adhiratha with his arrows, yet slew your sons.

sanskrit: sa vāryamāṇo bhīmena śitair bāṇaiḥ samantataḥ sūtaputro mahārāja bhīmasenam avaikṣata
english: Though held off on every side by Bhīma's sharp arrows, the son of the sūta, O great king, kept his gaze fixed upon Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: taṃ bhīmasenaḥ saṃrambhāt krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ visphārya sumahac cāpaṃ muhuḥ karṇam avaikṣata
english: And Bhīmasena, in his fury, his eyes red with wrath, drawing his vast bow taut, gazed again and again upon Karṇa.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tavātmajāṃs tu patitān dṛṣṭvā karṇaḥ pratāpavān krodhena mahatāviṣṭo nirviṇṇo 'bhūt sa jīvitāt
english: Saṃjaya said: When valiant Karṇa saw your sons fallen, he was seized with a great wrath and grew weary of his own life.

sanskrit: āgaskṛtam ivātmānaṃ mene cādhirathis tadā bhīmasenaṃ tataḥ kruddhaḥ samādravata saṃbhramāt
english: The son of Adhiratha then deemed himself an offender, as it were; and in his anger he rushed upon Bhīmasena in haste.

sanskrit: sa bhīmaṃ pañcabhir viddhvā rādheyaḥ prahasann iva punar vivyādha saptatyā svarṇapuṅkhaiḥ śilāśitaiḥ
english: Rādheya, having pierced Bhīma with five shafts as though with a smile, struck him again with seventy arrows golden-nocked and whetted on stone.

sanskrit: avahāsaṃ tu taṃ pārtho nāmṛṣyata vṛkodaraḥ tato vivyādha rādheyaṃ śatena nataparvaṇām
english: But Vṛkodara, son of Pṛthā, would not brook that mockery, and pierced Rādheya in turn with a hundred smooth-jointed shafts.

sanskrit: punaś ca viśikhais tīkṣṇair viddhvā pañcabhir āśugaiḥ dhanuś ciccheda bhallena sūtaputrasya māriṣa
english: And again, having pierced him with five swift, keen arrows, he cut asunder the bow of the sūta's son with a broad-headed shaft, O honored one.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya karṇo bhārata durmanāḥ iṣubhiś chādayām āsa bhīmasenaṃ samantataḥ
english: Then Karṇa, taking up another bow, O Bhārata, sore at heart, covered Bhīmasena on every side with his arrows.

sanskrit: tasya bhīmo hayān hatvā vinihatya ca sārathim prajahāsa mahāhāsaṃ kṛte pratikṛtaṃ punaḥ
english: But Bhīma, having slain his horses and struck down his charioteer, laughed a great laugh, the deed repaid once more.

sanskrit: iṣubhiḥ kārmukaṃ cāsya cakarta puruṣarṣabhaḥ tat papāta mahārāja svarṇapṛṣṭhaṃ mahāsvanam
english: And that bull among men cut his bow apart with arrows; it fell, O great king, gold-backed and loud-resounding.

sanskrit: avārohad rathāt tasmād atha karṇo mahārathaḥ gadāṃ gṛhītvā samare bhīmasenāya cākṣipat
english: Then Karṇa, that mighty car-warrior, descended from his chariot, and seizing a mace, hurled it at Bhīmasena in the fray.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ sahasā gadāṃ dṛṣṭvā vṛkodaraḥ śarair avārayad rājan sarvasainyasya paśyataḥ
english: Seeing that mace come hurtling suddenly upon him, Vṛkodara warded it off with his arrows, O king, in the sight of the whole army.

sanskrit: tato bāṇasahasrāṇi preṣayām āsa pāṇḍavaḥ sūtaputravadhākāṅkṣī tvaramāṇaḥ parākramī
english: Then the valiant son of Pāṇḍu, eager to slay the sūta's son, sent forth in haste thousands of arrows.

sanskrit: tān iṣūn iṣubhiḥ karṇo vārayitvā mahāmṛdhe kavacaṃ bhīmasenasya pātayām āsa sāyakaiḥ
english: Warding off those shafts with his own arrows in that great battle, Karṇa with his darts struck down the armor of Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: athainaṃ pañcaviṃśatyā kṣudrakāṇāṃ samārpayat paśyatāṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Then he pierced him with twenty-five small arrows; and to all beings who beheld it, that seemed a wondrous thing.

sanskrit: tato bhīmo mahārāja navabhir nataparvaṇām raṇe 'preṣayata kruddhaḥ sūtaputrasya māriṣa
english: Then Bhīma, O great king, in his wrath sent against the sūta's son in battle nine smooth-jointed shafts, O honored one.

sanskrit: te tasya kavacaṃ bhittvā tathā bāhuṃ ca dakṣiṇam abhyagur dharaṇīṃ tīkṣṇā valmīkam iva pannagāḥ
english: Piercing his armor and his right arm, those keen shafts entered the earth like serpents entering an anthill.

sanskrit: rādheyaṃ tu raṇe dṛṣṭvā padātinam avasthitam bhīmasenena saṃrabdhaṃ rājā duryodhano 'bravīt tvaradhvaṃ sarvato yattā rādheyasya rathaṃ prati
english: But seeing Rādheya standing on foot in the battle, sore beset by Bhīmasena, King Duryodhana said: 'Make haste, all of you, intent and ready, to bring a chariot to Rādheya.'

sanskrit: tatas tava sutā rājañ śrutvā bhrātur vaco drutam abhyayuḥ pāṇḍavaṃ yuddhe visṛjantaḥ śitāñ śarān
english: Then your sons, O king, hearing their brother's word, swiftly advanced against the son of Pāṇḍu in battle, loosing keen arrows.

sanskrit: citropacitraś citrākṣaś cārucitraḥ śarāsanaḥ citrāyudhaś citravarmā samare citrayodhinaḥ
english: Citra, Upacitra, Citrākṣa, Cārucitra, Śarāsana, Citrāyudha, and Citravarman—warriors of wondrous skill in battle.

sanskrit: āgacchatas tān sahasā bhīmo rājan mahārathaḥ sāśvasūtadhvajān yattān pātayām āsa saṃyuge te hatā nyapatan bhūmau vātanunnā iva drumāḥ
english: As they came on swiftly, Bhīma, that mighty car-warrior, O king, struck them down in the fray together with their horses, charioteers, and standards; slain, they fell to the earth like trees felled by the wind.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā vinihatān putrāṃs tava rājan mahārathān aśrupūrṇamukhaḥ karṇaḥ kaśmalaṃ samapadyata
english: Seeing your sons, those mighty car-warriors, slain, O king, Karṇa, his face full of tears, fell into a swoon of grief.

sanskrit: ratham anyaṃ samāsthāya vidhivat kalpitaṃ punaḥ abhyayāt pāṇḍavaṃ yuddhe tvaramāṇaḥ parākramī
english: Mounting another chariot duly equipped, the valiant one again advanced in haste against the son of Pāṇḍu in battle.

sanskrit: tāv anyonyaṃ śarair viddhvā svarṇapuṅkhaiḥ śilāśitaiḥ vyabhrājetāṃ mahārāja puṣpitāv iva kiṃśukau
english: Piercing each other with arrows golden-nocked and whetted on stone, the two shone, O great king, like a pair of kiṃśuka trees in flower.

sanskrit: ṣaṭtriṃśadbhis tato bhallair niśitais tigmatejanaiḥ vyadhamat kavacaṃ kruddhaḥ sūtaputrasya pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Then the son of Pāṇḍu, in his wrath, with thirty-six sharp broad-headed shafts of fierce point, shattered the armor of the sūta's son.

sanskrit: raktacandanadigdhāṅgau śaraiḥ kṛtamahāvraṇau śoṇitāktau vyarājetāṃ kālasūryāv ivoditau
english: Their limbs as if smeared with red sandal, deeply wounded by arrows and bathed in blood, the two shone like twin suns of the world's end newly risen.

sanskrit: tau śoṇitokṣitair gātraiḥ śaraiś chinnatanucchadau vivarmāṇau vyarājetāṃ nirmuktāv iva pannagau
english: With their bodies drenched in blood, their armor riven by arrows, the two, stripped of mail, shone like serpents that had cast their slough.

sanskrit: vyāghrāv iva naravyāghrau daṃṣṭrābhir itaretaram śaradaṃṣṭrā vidhunvānau tatakṣatur ariṃdamau
english: Like two tigers tearing each other with their fangs, those tamers of foes, those tigers among men, brandishing arrows for fangs, rent one another.

sanskrit: vāraṇāv iva saṃsaktau raṅgamadhye virejatuḥ tudantau viśikhais tīkṣṇair mattavāraṇavikramau
english: Locked together like two elephants, they shone in the midst of the field, striking each other with keen shafts, in prowess like rutting elephants.

sanskrit: pracchādayantau samare śarajālaiḥ parasparam rathābhyāṃ nādayantau ca diśaḥ sarvā viceratuḥ
english: Covering each other in battle with nets of arrows, and making all the quarters resound with their chariots, the two ranged about.

sanskrit: tau rathābhyāṃ mahārāja maṇḍalāvartanādiṣu vyarocetāṃ mahātmānau vṛtravajradharāv iva
english: With their chariots, O great king, in wheeling rounds and like maneuvers, those two high-souled ones shone like Vṛtra and the wielder of the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: sahastābharaṇābhyāṃ tu bhujābhyāṃ vikṣipan dhanuḥ vyarocata raṇe bhīmaḥ savidyud iva toyadaḥ
english: Drawing his bow with arms adorned with bracelets, Bhīma shone in the battle like a thunderhead lit with lightning.

sanskrit: sa cāpaghoṣastanitaḥ śaradhārāmbudo mahān bhīmamegho mahārāja karṇaparvatam abhyayāt
english: Thundering with the roar of his bow, that great rain-cloud of arrow-showers, the dread cloud that was Bhīma, O great king, advanced upon the mountain that was Karṇa.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarasahasreṇa dhanurmuktena bhārata pāṇḍavo vyakirat karṇaṃ ghano 'drim iva vṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: Then with a thousand arrows loosed from his bow, O Bhārata, the son of Pāṇḍu covered Karṇa as a cloud covers a mountain with its rains.

sanskrit: tatrāvaikṣanta putrās te bhīmasenasya vikramam supuṅkhaiḥ kaṅkavāsobhir yat karṇaṃ chādayac charaiḥ
english: There your sons beheld the valor of Bhīmasena, who covered Karṇa with shafts fair-nocked and fledged with heron's feathers.

sanskrit: sa nandayan raṇe pārthaṃ keśavaṃ ca yaśasvinam sātyakiṃ cakrarakṣau ca bhīmaḥ karṇam ayodhayat
english: Gladdening the son of Pṛthā in battle, and the glorious Keśava, and Sātyaki and the two guardians of the wheels, Bhīma fought against Karṇa.

sanskrit: vikramaṃ bhujayor vīryaṃ dhairyaṃ ca viditātmanaḥ putrās tava mahārāja dadṛśuḥ pāṇḍavasya ha
english: The prowess of his arms, the valor and the steadfastness of that self-possessed hero—your sons, O great king, beheld it all in the son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca bhīmasenasya rādheyaḥ śrutvā jyātalanisvanam nāmṛṣyata yathā matto gajaḥ pratigajasvanam
english: Saṃjaya said: When Rādheya heard the twang of Bhīmasena's bowstring and the slap of his palm, he brooked it no more, as a rutting elephant brooks not the trumpeting of a rival.

sanskrit: apakramya sa bhīmasya muhūrtaṃ śaragocarāt tava cādhirathir dṛṣṭvā syandanebhyaś cyutān sutān
english: Withdrawing for a moment from the range of Bhīma's arrows, the son of Adhiratha beheld your sons fallen from their chariots.

sanskrit: bhīmasenena nihatān vimanā duḥkhito 'bhavat niḥśvasan dīrgham uṣṇaṃ ca punaḥ pāṇḍavam abhyayāt
english: Slain by Bhīmasena, they lay there; downcast and grieved, sighing long and hot, he again advanced upon the son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: sa tāmranayanaḥ krodhāc chvasann iva mahoragaḥ babhau karṇaḥ śarān asyan raśmivān iva bhāskaraḥ
english: His eyes red as copper with wrath, hissing like a great serpent, Karṇa, loosing his arrows, blazed like the radiant sun shedding its beams.

sanskrit: raśmijālair ivārkasya vitatair bharatarṣabha karṇacāpacyutair bāṇaiḥ prācchādyata vṛkodaraḥ
english: As if by the spreading webs of the sun's rays, O bull of the Bharatas, Vṛkodara was overspread by the arrows loosed from Karṇa's bow.

sanskrit: karṇacāpacyutāś citrāḥ śarā barhiṇavāsasaḥ viviśuḥ sarvataḥ pārthaṃ vāsāyevāṇḍajā drumam
english: The bright arrows fledged with peacock-feathers, loosed from Karṇa's bow, entered the son of Pṛthā from every side, as birds settle upon a tree to roost.

sanskrit: karṇacāpacyutā bāṇāḥ saṃpatantas tatas tataḥ rukmapuṅkhā vyarājanta haṃsāḥ śreṇīkṛtā iva
english: The golden-nocked arrows loosed from Karṇa's bow, flying hither and thither, shone like wild geese ranged in rows.

sanskrit: cāpadhvajopaskarebhyaś chatrād īṣāmukhād yugāt prabhavanto vyadṛśyanta rājann ādhiratheḥ śarāḥ
english: Springing forth, as it seemed, from his bow, his banner, and the gear of his car, from his parasol, from the shaft-end of the pole, and from the yoke, the arrows of Adhiratha's son were seen, O king.

sanskrit: khaṃ pūrayan mahāvegān khagamān khagavāsasaḥ suvarṇavikṛtāṃś citrān mumocādhirathiḥ śarān
english: Filling the sky, the son of Adhiratha let fly his arrows of great speed, sky-coursing and feather-fledged, bright and wrought with gold.

sanskrit: tam antakam ivāyastam āpatantaṃ vṛkodaraḥ tyaktvā prāṇān abhikrudhya vivyādha navabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: As he bore down like Death himself strained for the kill, Vṛkodara, with his own life held cheap and burning with wrath, pierced him with nine arrows.

sanskrit: tasya vegam asaṃsahyaṃ dṛṣṭvā karṇasya pāṇḍavaḥ mahataś ca śaraughāṃs tān naivāvyathata vīryavān
english: Seeing the unbearable onslaught of Karṇa and those great floods of arrows, the valiant son of Pāṇḍu was not in the least dismayed.

sanskrit: tato vidhamyādhiratheḥ śarajālāni pāṇḍavaḥ vivyādha karṇaṃ viṃśatyā punar anyaiḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then, scattering the nets of arrows of Adhiratha's son, the son of Pāṇḍu pierced Karṇa with twenty more keen shafts.

sanskrit: yathaiva hi śaraiḥ pārthaḥ sūtaputreṇa chāditaḥ tathaiva karṇaṃ samare chādayām āsa pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Even as the son of Pṛthā had been covered with arrows by the sūta's son, so too did the son of Pāṇḍu cover Karṇa in the battle.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu bhīmasenasya vikramaṃ yudhi bhārata abhyanandaṃs tvadīyāś ca saṃprahṛṣṭāś ca cāraṇāḥ
english: Beholding the valor of Bhīmasena in battle, O Bhārata, your own people and the celestial bards rejoiced and applauded with delight.

sanskrit: bhūriśravāḥ kṛpo drauṇir madrarājo jayadrathaḥ uttamaujā yudhāmanyuḥ sātyakiḥ keśavārjunau
english: Bhūriśravas, Kṛpa, the son of Droṇa, the king of the Madras, Jayadratha, Uttamaujas, Yudhāmanyu, Sātyaki, Keśava, and Arjuna—

sanskrit: kurupāṇḍavānāṃ pravarā daśa rājan mahārathāḥ sādhu sādhv iti vegena siṃhanādam athānadan
english: these ten foremost mighty car-warriors among the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas, O king, crying 'Well done! Well done!' raised forthwith a mighty lion's roar.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu tumule śabde pravṛtte lomaharṣaṇe abhyabhāṣata putrāṃs te rājan duryodhanas tvaran
english: While that tumultuous, hair-raising clamor arose, O king, Duryodhana hastily addressed your sons.

sanskrit: rājñaś ca rājaputrāṃś ca sodaryāṃś ca viśeṣataḥ karṇaṃ gacchata bhadraṃ vaḥ parīpsanto vṛkodarāt
english: To the kings and the princes, and his own brothers especially: 'Go to Karṇa—good fortune to you—seeking to deliver him from Vṛkodara.'

sanskrit: purā nighnanti rādheyaṃ bhīmacāpacyutāḥ śarāḥ te yatadhvaṃ maheṣvāsāḥ sūtaputrasya rakṣaṇe
english: 'Before the arrows loosed from Bhīma's bow strike down Rādheya, exert yourselves, O great archers, to guard the sūta's son.'

sanskrit: duryodhanasamādiṣṭāḥ sodaryāḥ sapta māriṣa bhīmasenam abhidrutya saṃrabdhāḥ paryavārayan
english: At Duryodhana's command, seven of his brothers, O honored one, rushed furiously upon Bhīmasena and surrounded him.

sanskrit: te samāsādya kaunteyam āvṛṇvañ śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ parvataṃ vāridhārābhiḥ prāvṛṣīva balāhakāḥ
english: Closing in upon the son of Kuntī, they enveloped him with showers of arrows, as rain-clouds in the wet season enwrap a mountain with their torrents.

sanskrit: te 'pīḍayan bhīmasenaṃ kruddhāḥ sapta mahārathāḥ prajāsaṃharaṇe rājan somaṃ sapta grahā iva
english: Those seven mighty car-warriors in their wrath beset Bhīmasena, O king, as the seven planets beset the moon at the time of the dissolution of beings.

sanskrit: tato vāmena kaunteyaḥ pīḍayitvā śarāsanam muṣṭinā pāṇḍavo rājan dṛḍhena supariṣkṛtam
english: Then the son of Kuntī, the son of Pāṇḍu, gripping his bow tightly in his firm left fist, O king—that well-wrought bow—

sanskrit: manuṣyasamatāṃ jñātvā sapta saṃdhāya sāyakān tebhyo vyasṛjad āyastaḥ sūryaraśminibhān prabhuḥ
english: and judging them but men like himself, fitted seven arrows like the sun's own beams, and the mighty one, drawing them taut, loosed them upon those foes.

sanskrit: nirasyann iva dehebhyas tanayānām asūṃs tava bhīmaseno mahārāja pūrvavairam anusmaran
english: As if casting forth the very life-breaths from the bodies of your sons, Bhīmasena, O great king, remembered the old enmity.

sanskrit: te kṣiptā bhīmasenena śarā bhārata bhāratān vidārya khaṃ samutpetuḥ svarṇapuṅkhāḥ śilāśitāḥ
english: Those arrows hurled by Bhīmasena, O Bhārata, golden-nocked and whetted on stone, having pierced the Bhāratas, sprang up into the sky.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ vidārya cetāṃsi śarā hemavibhūṣitāḥ vyarājanta mahārāja suparṇā iva khecarāḥ
english: Having rent open their hearts, those gold-adorned arrows shone, O great king, like sky-coursing eagles.

sanskrit: śoṇitādigdhavājāgrāḥ sapta hemapariṣkṛtāḥ putrāṇāṃ tava rājendra pītvā śoṇitam udgatāḥ
english: Their feathered tips smeared with blood, those seven gold-wrought shafts, O lord of kings, sprang up again, having drunk the blood of your sons.

sanskrit: te śarair bhinnamarmāṇo rathebhyaḥ prāpatan kṣitau girisānuruhā bhagnā dvipeneva mahādrumāḥ
english: Their vital parts pierced by the arrows, they fell from their chariots to the earth, like great trees grown on mountain ridges, broken by an elephant.

sanskrit: śatruṃjayaḥ śatrusahaś citraś citrāyudho dṛḍhaḥ citraseno vikarṇaś ca saptaite vinipātitāḥ
english: Śatruṃjaya, Śatrusaha, Citra, Citrāyudha, Dṛḍha, Citrasena, and Vikarṇa—these seven were laid low.

sanskrit: tān nihatya mahābāhū rādheyasyaiva paśyataḥ siṃhanādaravaṃ ghoram asṛjat pāṇḍunandanaḥ
english: Having slain them, the mighty-armed son of Pāṇḍu, before the very eyes of Rādheya, sent forth a terrible roar like a lion's.

sanskrit: sa ravas tasya śūrasya dharmarājasya bhārata ācakhyāv iva tad yuddhaṃ vijayaṃ cātmano mahat
english: That roar of the hero, O Bhārata, seemed to proclaim to the King of Righteousness that battle and his own great victory.
